concept.name: Higher high
concept.definition: A swing high that exceeds the previous swing high. A sequence of higher highs combined with higher lows is the classical structural definition of an uptrend.
concept.intuition: Each upward push reaches new territory, showing buyers keep gaining ground.
concept.mechanics: Identified by comparing successive reaction peaks: when the latest peak trades or closes above the prior peak, a higher high is printed. Analysts track the sequence of highs and lows, rather than any single point, to judge whether trend structure remains intact.
concept.failure_modes: A single higher high can be an exhaustion spike; without confirming higher lows the apparent bullish structure can invert immediately.
concept.misconceptions: That printing one higher high confirms an uptrend; structure is a property of a sequence, and one peak in isolation means little.
concept.example: After a pullback, a stock rallies past its old 55 peak to 58, printing a higher high that keeps the uptrend structure intact.
